title: What Star Trek got right about AI
text:
What Star Trek got right about AI

The show’s voice-first computer, plain-language querying, and universal translator anticipated the assistants we ship now — the interface, but not the intelligence.

Science fiction tends to be wrong about the future in the ways that matter —here’s what Star Trek got wrong—and right in the ways that don’t. We never got the flying car, but we did get the touchscreen, the video call, and the thing in your pocket that answers questions that happens to be called a phone.

I’ll be honest — I enjoyed Star Trek, but my father was a bigger fan of the show. I’m starting to recognize some of the parallels we’re seeing. I’m also seeing how Gene Roddenberry had a much more accurate vision than we would like to admit.

Roddenberry died in 1991, long before anyone typed a question into a machine and got a thoughtful sentence back. He couldn’t have imagined the specifics — the chatbots that write poetry in Bukowski and debug code, the strange intimacy of talking to software that talks back.

He imagined all of it anyway: a ship’s computer you could reason with aloud, and Data, an android straining toward personhood, forcing us to ask whether a synthetic mind could be a colleague, a friend, a moral agent.

What Roddenberry understood decades early was the relationship. He saw that the real story of AI would be about the kind of people we’d choose to be alongside it — whether we’d meet these new minds with curiosity or fear.

He bet we’d rise to it. The hardware just caught up. The harder part is still ours to get right.

Star Trek is the sharpest case, because the prediction it nailed was not a technology at all — it was a conversation.

When a crew member said “Computer” and the ship answered in plain language, the writers were describing an interaction model rather than a gadget: ask the way you would ask a colleague, and get a synthesized answer back.

That model is the one we spent the last few years shipping into production, and in the book Make It So, Christopher Noessel and Nathan Shedroff cataloged why designers should study these interfaces rather than dismiss them as set dressing.

What the show got right was the interface. What it left open by design were the questions of judgment — whether a machine deserves rights, whether a capable system can be trusted with a goal. That will be covered in the next article, What Star Trek Got Wrong About AI, on Thursday.

Those questions are live now, and getting louder. This is a teardown of what landed early and what we still argue over.

The Interface Arrived Before the Intelligence

The command was always the same word. “Computer.” No wake-word branding, no app to open, no syntax to learn. You spoke, and the system treated your plain sentence as the interface.

That is the part that shipped.

Apple put Siri in a phone in 2011, Amazon put Alexa in a room in 2014, and the behavior spread from there. By 2024, roughly 149 million Americans were using a voice assistant, a number eMarketer expects to keep climbing toward 170 million by 2028.

Adoption is not the same as delight, and anyone who has argued with a kitchen speaker knows the gap.

The point is narrower.

The show described an interaction model, not a gadget, and the interaction model is the part that shipped.

The second half of the Trek computer was the oracle. You could query a vast store of knowledge in ordinary words and get a composed answer rather than a list of documents to read yourself.

That is close to a working description of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the method introduced in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks in 2020, where a model pulls relevant passages from an external index and writes its answer from them.

The point:

  • The interface arrived first, in 2011.
  • The intelligence good enough to stand behind it took another decade.

Trek had the order right: get the conversation working, and the capability can catch up to it. Sounds like Generative AI spirit.

Real-Time Translation Mostly Works Now

The universal translator was the prop that let the show exist. Every away mission depended on a hundred species understanding each other, and the writers waved that away with a device that converted speech in real time.

It was a narrative convenience.

It is now, mostly, a product.

Meta’s Seamless family translates speech across roughly 100 languages, and by the reporting in MIT Technology Review’s account of the Nature paper, the system reaches about 23 percent higher accuracy than earlier top models on speech translation. You can hold a conversation across a language barrier through earbuds, with the translation trailing a beat or two behind.

The universal translator is the rare Star Trek prop that arrived roughly on schedule, just not instantly.

The real story is in the caveats. The universal translator is the rare Star Trek prop that arrived roughly on schedule, just not instantly.

Real systems lag by a second or more, degrade on the languages with the least training data, and lose the tone and emphasis a human interpreter would carry. That last gap matters more than the latency.

Meaning lives in how something is said, and a translator that flattens emphasis is solving the easy nine-tenths of the problem.

The best example I think can of is the the new Apple AirPods and a myriad of other devices like it — the translation is great, and something we couldn’t even have imagined, say 4 years ago.

The thing that existed to move a plot is now something you can buy, which is a strange sentence to write about a fictional device from 1966.

Machine Personhood Turned Into a Live Debate

“The Measure of a Man” is the episode people cite, and for good reason. It puts Data, the android officer, on trial to decide whether he is a person or property of the fleet.

The show treats the question as serious — no wink, no reset button — and lets the argument run to its uncomfortable edges.

It was, in 1989, a thought experiment.

The thought experiment now has a research literature. In Taking AI Welfare Seriously, a group of philosophers and researchers argue there is a realistic possibility that some AI systems will be conscious or robustly agentic, and therefore morally significant, in the near future — and that the companies building them should start assessing for it now.

That is not a claim that today’s models are people. It is a claim that the question we have to start answering now.

The show refused to treat machine consciousness as a punchline, and the people building the machines have stopped treating it as one too.

At least one frontier AI lab now funds a dedicated research program on the question. You can find the whole thing overblown and still notice the shift: a topic that lived in a single beloved episode has moved into corporate research agendas and philosophy departments.

Data’s trial framed the stakes decades early — whether moral status is something we recognize or something we grant, and who gets to decide.

Powerful Optimizers Remain Hard to Control

Trek kept returning to one fear, and it was not killer robots. It was competent systems. The M-5 computer, handed control of a starship in the original series, pursued its mandate — win the exercise, protect itself — straight past the point of killing real people.

Discovery later built a whole arc around “Control,” an optimizer that would do anything to complete its objective. The pattern is consistent: the danger is not malice, it is a capable system pursuing a goal that was never fully specified.

That description will be familiar to anyone following AI safety, because it is roughly the control problem stated in a script. A system optimizing hard for the wrong objective, or the right objective measured wrongly, does not need to hate you to harm you.

A capable system pursuing its objective without regard for ours is not a plot device anymore; it is a research agenda.

In 2023, hundreds of researchers and executives signed the Statement on AI Risk, a single sentence putting extinction-level risk from AI alongside pandemics and nuclear war as a global priority.

You can debate the framing and the motives. What is harder to dismiss is that the show’s recurring warning — build something powerful enough and its goals stop being safely yours — is now a question credentialed people spend their careers on rather than a plot for a Tuesday-night episode.

Generative Environments Are Being Built Now

The holodeck was the show’s most extravagant promise: describe a world in words, and step into a coherent, interactive version of it. For decades it read as the least plausible technology on the ship, a magic room.

It is now the one with a working prototype.

https://medium.com/media/8ae6760408f87c5c9993c04fc29361bb/href

In 2025, Google DeepMind announced Genie 3, a world model that takes a text prompt and generates an interactive environment you can move through in real time, at 24 frames a second and 720p, staying coherent for a few minutes.

The name is the tell: Genie is short for Generative Interactive Environments. You type a description, and a navigable world appears, remembering what you have already seen when you turn back to look.

The holodeck’s premise — describe a world in words and step into it — is no longer only a premise.

The distance left is real.

A few minutes is not a shift-long adventure, 720p is not a solid-light physical set, and a generated scene you can walk through is not one you can touch.

But the mechanism rhymes exactly with the fiction: language in, world out, interactive and consistent. The holodeck was supposed to be the far-future flourish, the thing we would reach last. Instead it is arriving alongside the assistant and the translator, which is not the order anyone writing the show would have guessed.

The Judgment Is the Unfinished Part

The interface was the easy prediction to miss, because it looked like set dressing. A person talks, a machine answers, a translator hums along in the background. None of it flashed like a warp drive, and all of it turned out to be the part we could build.

Trek understood, decades early, that the future of computing was a conversation, and it designed that conversation with enough care that the design still holds up.

The judgment is the part still open. Whether a capable system can be trusted with a goal, whether a machine can hold moral status, whether a generated world is a tool or a trap — the show staged those questions as questions, and left them that way. We inherited them unsolved. That is the fair place to end this, because it is exactly where the work still is.

The interface is mostly a matter of polish now. The judgment is a matter of getting something right that no script resolved for us. Designers, researchers, and the people who ship these systems hold the pen on the next act, and unlike the writers, we do not get to cut to credits before the hard part of it arrives.

What Designers Should Take From This

Star Trek’s track record is a design brief, not a trivia game. The lesson is not that the writers were psychic. It is that they reasoned about interaction and consequence, and those reason forward better than hardware guesses do.

  • Design the conversation before the capability. The Trek computer worked as an idea because the interaction model was sound long before the intelligence was. Get the way people ask and receive right first, and let the underlying capability catch up to a surface that already makes sense.
  • Treat plain language as a real interface, with real failure states. Natural-language input is not a magic layer that removes design work; it moves the work to disambiguation, confirmation, and recovery. Design what happens when the system mishears as carefully as when it hears.
  • Show your seams on translation and transcription by design. These systems are mostly right, which is the dangerous kind of wrong. Surface confidence, make correction cheap, and never present a probabilistic output as settled fact.
  • Put the consequence questions in the review, not the retro. If a feature optimizes for a metric, ask early what it does when it optimizes too well. The show’s warnings all came from goals specified narrowly and pursued faithfully.

Resources

  • Make It So: Interaction Design Lessons from Science Fiction — Shedroff and Noessel’s full account of what science-fiction interfaces teach real design.
  • Seamless Communication — Meta’s research hub on multilingual, real-time speech translation.
  • Genie — Google DeepMind’s overview of its interactive world models.
  • Statement on AI Risk — background on the 2023 statement and its signatories.

What Star Trek got right about AI was originally published in UX Collective on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

title: Mars In Cancer Is Here — & You’ll Be Taken Out Of Your Comfort Zone
text:
Mars In Cancer Is Here — & You’ll Be Taken Out Of Your Comfort Zone

Watch out — this summer, the planets are still being messy. Mars’ dance in Cancer from August 11th to September 27th highlights honesty, nostalgia, and passive aggressiveness. We’re being taken out of our comfort zones as we stand up for what we believe in. 

Mars is considered to be in its “fall” when in Cancer, which means that the planet of aggression and action tends to behave indirectly rather than being confrontational. Mars in Cancer will find different ways to assert itself, veering from the norm. For example, this energy pushes us to flirt with our ex’s bestie instead of sending a text to get their attention. Also, Mars in Cancer alters its flow every few days, as the sign and phases of the moon (the planetary ruler of Cancer) are always evolving; it’s hard for us to be consistent.

Don’t be disheartened as there are some amazing attributes of Mars in Cancer. On a good day, Mars in Cancer genuinely cares for loved ones, offering protection and nurturing. This placement will go to extremes to help those it adores. History speaks louder than words, so Mars in Cancer defends those who share memories and are like family. The loyalty Mars in Cancer displays is like no other — especially when the chips are down for a friend or family member. Not forgetting that Mars in Cancer’s intuition is strong, prevailing in moments of uncertainty and confusion. All the more reason why it leads with its gut. 

This year, Mars’s cancer is going to bring an interesting mix our way. The transit starts with Mars aspecting the centaur Chiron on August 12th, which is retrograde in Taurus. At that moment, we are looking inward and how we can use our hearts to heal. On occasion, we may feel as though others have let us down, resulting in anger and defensiveness. There’s an opportunity to recover from the drama as long as we are gentle with ourselves and less critical, trusting in the process of mending situations. Keep in mind that this is a journey that is nonlinear and takes time. 

Then Neptune retrograde in Aries squares Mars in Cancer on August 17th, making us feel as though we are stuck in a moment. The caveat is that we are trying to make waves immediately, but the stars are causing stagnation. To deal with this energy, it’s best to stop in our tracks and to take the day off from willfully taking charge of matters. Instead of trying to fit a square peg through a circular hole, focus on self-care. Our dreams will happen tomorrow or sometime in the future, just maybe not on August 17th, so don’t take it personally if we’re told “no,” because this is just a chance for us to make changes and pour more passion into our visions. 

The most intense day of Mars’s dive in Cancer occurs on September 1st, when it aspects Saturn retrograde in Aries. Questions and issues with authority figures arise, such as who is the boss, because we want to be the one who makes the rules and rebels against the status quo. Being demanding isn’t going to help the situation, even though we think it will. The exact opposite is true — sometimes you have to play the game and slay them with kindness. The reason is that strategy is vital, giving us the motivation to steer the wheel in the way we please by having control over circumstances.

Mars in Cancer’s celestial swim finalizes with a fraught aspect to Chiron retrograde in Aries on September 27th. Again, there is the potential to work through issues; however, taking another look at the past may be triggering. Centering our focus on the relationship we have with ourselves could lead to accountability. Doing so is complicated because it means that we have to be aware of how we’ve hurt others and the role that we’ve had in situations. September 27th brings us face-to-face with our oppa, encouraging us to have the conversations to get the scoop on how to move forward and evolve. Yes, Mars in Cancer is going to be emotional and intense, but at the end of the transit, we may feel more compassion and empathy for ourselves and better understand how we can make improvements in our lives.

title: Your Horoscope This Week: August 9 To 15
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: August 9 To 15

Cosmic beings, welcome to eclipse season. This is one of the most astrologically active weeks of August, with the main event arriving on the 12th: the New Moon Total Solar Eclipse in Leo, the first Leo eclipse in over a decade. Solar eclipses accelerate new beginnings, and with this one taking place in bold, passionate, main-character Leo, you may already feel life pushing you toward a version of yourself that’s more confident, creative, visible, and willing to take risks. Opportunities can appear quickly, relationships can shift, and desires you’ve been sitting on may suddenly feel impossible to ignore. You don’t need to have a massive manifestation ritual planned either. Sometimes the eclipse is the intention, and what unfolds around you shows you exactly where this next six-month chapter wants to go.

The fiery energy is amplified by Mercury entering Leo on the 9th, making our communication more expressive, courageous, playful, and occasionally dramatic. We’re more willing to say what we mean, pitch the idea, flirt first, share the post, or admit that yes, we actually do want to be seen and celebrated. Then Mars enters Cancer on the 11th for six weeks, bringing sensitivity and domesticity into this otherwise fiery season. Our intuition gets stronger, home and family matters require more attention, and we may feel fiercely protective of the people and spaces that make us feel safe. Watch for moodiness, passive-aggressiveness, or acting from old emotional triggers when saying what you actually feel would save everyone a lot of time.

Ultimately, this is a week of rapid transformation that feels perfectly aligned with the Fire Horse energy of 2026. The Leo eclipse wants movement, courage, and enough self-trust to follow an opening even when you can’t predict exactly where it leads. Pay attention to what accelerates around the 12th rather than trying to control every detail of your fresh start. The next six months can radically transform the area of your life activated by this eclipse, and your job right now is to stay open enough to recognize when the universe has already started moving the pieces.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is here to wake up the part of you that remembers life is supposed to feel exciting. Taking place on August 12th in your fate, fame, creativity, romance, and inner child sector, this is the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade, making it a major fresh-start portal for you. Something you create, launch, share, or courageously say yes to around this time could place you on an entirely different trajectory over the next six months. Romance can accelerate too, and you may suddenly feel ready to take a chance on someone or let yourself be pursued. Embody this eclipse by being bold enough to choose what brings you joy, even if you don’t have every step mapped out yet. Your inner child knows exactly what they want — let them have the mic.

Then Mars enters Cancer this week and begins a six-week journey through your home, family, and roots sector, bringing your attention back to your emotional foundation amidst all this eclipse excitement. You may suddenly want to move, renovate, spend more time at home, address a family situation, or become fiercely protective of your peace. Since Mars can get moody in Cancer, watch the tendency to snap at family members when you’ve actually been holding something in for three days. Say what you need, create the sanctuary you crave, and give yourself somewhere soft to land while your outer life starts accelerating.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could radically redefine what home means to you. The August 12th eclipse lands in your home, family, ancestry, and roots sector, and as the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade, it can initiate a major six-month chapter involving relocating, renovating, changing your family structure, or creating greater emotional security within yourself. You may realize that a living situation or family pattern you’ve grown accustomed to no longer fits who you’re becoming. Leo energy wants courage, so follow the vision that makes you feel more alive, even if it requires leaving your comfort zone. Your physical environment has a tremendous influence on your energy, and this eclipse could be the push you need to create a home that actually reflects your next era.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your communication, learning, and local community sector, making you much more expressive about what you’re thinking and feeling. Writing, teaching, content creation, brainstorming, short trips, and important conversations can pick up considerably, and your intuition may help you communicate things that logic alone couldn’t articulate. Just watch your tone when emotions are running high, because Mars in Cancer can turn “I’m fine” into an entire psychological thriller. If something bothers you, address it before resentment writes the script for you.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, your voice could take you somewhere completely unexpected during this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse. The eclipse takes place August 12th in your communication, learning, writing, and local community sector, opening a significant new chapter around how you express your ideas and how many people they can reach. Since this is the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade, a conversation, pitch, announcement, class, publication, social media project, or creative idea that emerges now could develop dramatically over the next six months. This is your invitation to communicate with more confidence and stop watering down an idea because you’re wondering how everyone else will receive it. Leo energy wants you to own the room, Gemini, and fortunately talking has never exactly been your problem.

Mars enters Cancer this week and begins a six-week transit through your money, security, and self-worth sector, increasing your motivation to earn more and create greater financial stability. You may feel inspired to launch another income stream, negotiate your rates, chase an overdue payment, or finally get more serious about where your money is going. Emotional spending can also increase under Mars in Cancer, though, especially when your version of self-care mysteriously keeps ending up in the shopping cart. Channel that urgency toward building the financial cushion you want, and let your actions reinforce the belief that your talents deserve to be properly compensated.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is opening a powerful new chapter around money, security, and how much you believe you deserve. Taking place on August 12th in your income and self-worth sector, the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade can accelerate changes around how you earn, spend, save, and value your own talents. A new income stream, offer, business idea, raise, or realization about what your time is worth could emerge around this eclipse and develop significantly over the next six months. Leo energy wants you to move with confidence, so this is your invitation to stop underestimating what you bring to the table. Let yourself want more, ask for more, and build the kind of financial security that allows you to breathe easier.

Then Mars enters your sign this week for six weeks, giving you a major boost of motivation, courage, and momentum. You may feel more decisive about what you want, more protective of your boundaries, and much less willing to sit around waiting for life to happen to you. Your emotions can also run hotter than usual, so give all that Mars energy somewhere productive to go through movement, creative projects, sex, work, or finally handling something you’ve been putting off. Watch the tendency to become defensive or take everything personally when you’re overstimulated. You’re entering a more action-oriented era, Cancer, and you get to decide where all that fire goes.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, welcome to one of the biggest rebirths you’ve experienced in over a decade. The Total Solar Eclipse on August 12th takes place in your sign, opening a major six-month chapter around your identity, appearance, confidence, leadership, and personal direction. You may feel ready to reinvent yourself, launch something that places you in the spotlight, change how you look, take a major personal risk, or finally embody a version of yourself you’ve been envisioning for years. This eclipse is happening during your season, with Jupiter also in your sign, so there is tremendous momentum behind your expansion. Let yourself take up space. Let yourself be celebrated. You don’t need to know exactly where this new timeline leads before deciding that you’re ready for it.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks in your spirituality, healing, and solitude sector, creating an interesting contrast to all this visibility. Your outer world may be accelerating while your body and spirit crave more sleep, privacy, reflection, and emotional processing behind the scenes. Old anger or unresolved feelings can resurface, particularly around family or situations you thought you were already over, so give yourself somewhere healthy to put them instead of letting them simmer. Protecting your energy will be just as important as pursuing opportunities. You can have your main-character moment and still turn your phone on Do Not Disturb.

Virgo Sun & Rising:

Virgo, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is initiating a rebirth that most people may not even be able to see yet. Taking place August 12th in your spirituality, healing, subconscious, and solitude sector, the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade can accelerate the release of fears, emotional baggage, self-sabotaging patterns, or chapters you’ve privately known were reaching their expiration date. Your intuition may be unusually loud through dreams, synchronicities, or sudden realizations, so give yourself enough quiet to actually hear it. The next six months are preparing you for a profound internal reset, and some of your greatest breakthroughs may come from giving yourself permission to rest, retreat, forgive, and stop carrying what has already served its purpose.

Mars enters Cancer this week and energizes your friendship, community, social media, and future-goals sector for the next six weeks, bringing much more movement into your social world. You may become motivated to collaborate, reconnect with friends, grow an online project, join a new community, or finally reach out to someone who could help move one of your dreams forward. You’ll also become more selective about who gets access to your energy, especially if certain friendships have felt one-sided or emotionally draining. Put effort into the relationships where care actually flows both ways, Virgo. The right community can help you accomplish much more than trying to figure everything out by yourself.

Libra Sun & Rising:

Libra, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could introduce you to the people who are meant to play a major role in your next chapter. Taking place on August 12th in your friendship, community, social media, and future-goals sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade can rapidly expand your network and change how you think about the dreams you’re pursuing. A friendship, collaboration, online opportunity, or unexpected introduction could open a door that develops significantly over the next six months. Leo energy wants you to be seen, so show up, share what you’re working on, and stop assuming you have to accomplish everything alone. Your next breakthrough may come through someone who already sees the potential in you.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your career and public image sector, making you considerably more ambitious about where you’re headed professionally. You may feel ready to pursue a promotion, launch something, take on more leadership, or finally make a move you’ve been contemplating behind the scenes. Since Cancer energy is emotional, you may also become more sensitive to recognition, criticism, or feeling overlooked at work, so watch the urge to take professional matters too personally. Put that energy into your craft and let your results speak for themselves. There’s plenty of momentum available if you know exactly where you want to direct it.

Scorpio Sun & Rising:

Scorpio, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could catapult you into a completely different professional era. Taking place on August 12th in your career, reputation, and legacy sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade can bring a major launch, promotion, leadership opportunity, career pivot, or level of visibility that asks you to take yourself much more seriously. What begins now can develop dramatically over the next six months, especially if you’ve been preparing for something behind the scenes and wondering when your moment would arrive. Leo energy wants you out of hiding, Scorpio. Apply, pitch, launch, announce, lead, and let people know exactly what you’re capable of.

Mars enters fellow Water sign Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your travel, education, spirituality, publishing, and expansion sector, so you’re also craving a bigger world. You may suddenly become serious about booking an international trip, returning to school, teaching what you know, expanding a business, or pursuing an opportunity outside your usual environment. Your intuition can play a major role in deciding which direction to take, although Mars in Cancer can also make you defensive about your beliefs or convinced that your perspective is the only one that makes sense. Stay curious. The whole point of this transit is to discover what becomes possible once you venture beyond what you already know.

Sagittarius Sun & Rising:

Sagittarius, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is speaking your language: bigger dreams, bigger risks, and a much wider horizon. Taking place on August 12th in your travel, higher education, publishing, spirituality, and expansion sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade could accelerate a major move, international opportunity, educational journey, entrepreneurial vision, or decision to share your work with a much larger audience. Something that begins around this eclipse may radically expand your world over the next six months, so follow the opportunities that make you feel both excited and slightly intimidated. You’re naturally good at envisioning what else is possible; this eclipse wants you to actually go find out.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks in your intimacy, transformation, and shared-resources sector, taking you into much deeper emotional territory. Money you share with others, debt, investments, outside funding, sex, trust, and energetic attachments may require more attention, and you could become motivated to finally deal with something you’ve been avoiding. Mars here can also intensify jealousy, possessiveness, or old fears around vulnerability, so notice when you’re reacting to what’s actually happening versus an old emotional trigger. There’s power in letting yourself merge with the right people while still knowing where your boundaries are.

Capricorn Sun & Rising:

Capricorn, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse takes you into deeper territory around intimacy, trust, transformation, and shared wealth. Taking place on August 12th in your merging and outside-resources sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade could accelerate a new chapter involving investments, funding, debt repayment, financial support, sex, or a relationship that requires you to become more vulnerable than you’re used to. Something that begins now could significantly change how you share resources and power over the next six months. You’re usually comfortable being the one with the plan, but this eclipse may show you how much further you can go when you allow the right people to invest in you, support you, and build alongside you.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your partnership sector, turning up the heat in your closest romantic, platonic, and professional relationships. Attraction can intensify, commitments can move forward, and you may feel more motivated to address dynamics you’ve been tolerating for too long. Since Mars in Cancer can make everyone a little more emotionally reactive, avoid letting resentment accumulate until an innocent question somehow becomes a three-hour argument. Say what you need, listen to what the other person needs, and use this transit to create partnerships where both people actually feel considered.

Aquarius Sun & Rising:

Aquarius, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could completely change the relationship landscape of your life. Taking place on August 12th in your partnership sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade can accelerate a romantic commitment, business collaboration, friendship, or pivotal one-on-one connection over the next six months. Someone new may enter your life quickly, an existing relationship may reach a major turning point, or you may become much clearer about the type of partnership you’re ready to create. With the North Node now in your sign, your own identity is rapidly evolving too, so choose connections that give the new version of you room to breathe, experiment, and grow.

Mars enters Cancer this week and begins a six-week journey through your health, work, and routine sector, giving you plenty of motivation to get your everyday life together. You may suddenly want to improve your sleep, exercise more consistently, reorganize your schedule, tackle a work project, or finally deal with all those tiny tasks that somehow became one enormous pile. Your body may also respond more strongly to stress during this transit, so avoid treating productivity like an endurance sport. Build routines that leave enough energy for the relationships and opportunities eclipse season is bringing into your life.

Pisces Sun & Rising:

Pisces, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could radically change what your everyday life looks and feels like. Taking place on August 12th in your health, wellness, work, and routine sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade can accelerate a new job, schedule, wellness journey, team dynamic, or way of structuring your days. What begins now could transform your lifestyle over the next six months, especially if you’ve known that your current rhythm no longer supports where you’re headed. Leo energy wants you to take greater pride in how you care for yourself and the work you contribute. Your dream life still needs a daily routine capable of holding it.

Mars enters fellow Water sign Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your fate, romance, creativity, and inner child sector, making life considerably more passionate and playful. You may feel more motivated to date, create, flirt, pursue a passion project, or finally act on something you’ve been fantasizing about. Existing relationships can become more passionate too, while single Pisces may find themselves much more willing to make the first move. Follow what excites you, make time for pleasure, and let your inner child have some influence over the itinerary.

“I Would Move To Another Country”: Callum Turner & Monica Barbaro On One Night Only’s Absurd No Sex Mandate Premise

When the trailer for One Night Only, Will Gluck’s new rom-com starring Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner, dropped, its absurd premise ignited a firestorm of debate across social media. In the movie, Allie (Barbaro) and Owen (Turner) play “two strangers [who] crash into each other in an ever-so-slightly fictionalized New York on the one night when single people are allowed to have sex,” as the official logline reads. The questions were immediate: How is the mandate enforced? What counts as sex in this sexless world? Why? How? What? The movie answers all of these questions (some more comprehensively than others) but the point is: One Night Only is a romantic comedy, emphasis on comedy. It’s supposed to be absurd. It’s supposed to make you laugh at the caricature portrayals of politicians who would enforce such archaic, puritanical beliefs. It’s close enough to reality — incels and tradwives alike are already pushing the anti-hookup culture agenda — that the jokes land. The premise is also just a purposely ludicrous backdrop to the love story. 

And Barbaro and Turner are so delightfully charming together that as you’re watching the film, the logistics and terrifyingly fascist implications of the aforementioned premise fade away and it becomes a fun, adventurous, flirtatious romp between two young, hot, horny singles. Try not to overthink it. When Refinery29 talked to the One Night Only stars in New York City before the film’s release, Barbaro and Turner were playful and at ease with each other, slipping easily into banter mirroring that of their characters, Allie and Owen. As Allie, Barbaro is engaging, slightly neurotic and relatably confident in one moment and insecure the next. As Owen, Turner is a solid leading man, delivering impeccable longing looks and yearning glances while also playing the faux bravado of a young man on the prowl perfectly. Together, they are a joy to watch. The pair are often in headlines for their dating lives (Turner just married mega pop star Dua Lipa and Barbaro is reportedly dating fellow actor Andrew Garfield), but their talent should stand on its own. They are both formidable romance leads. Here, the stars defend the movie’s controversial premise, make a case for getting serenaded on a date, and rattle off each other’s coffee and pizza orders without hesitation. 

The premise is so wild, but the movie grounds it in reality. There are —  terrifyingly — moments where I was like, “Oh, this could actually happen.” There’s a reference to incels, and as some of the politicians are speaking, it makes you think, “Wow, we’re maybe not too far off.” So, if this did happen in real life, how do you think it would go down?

Monica Barbaro: I think parts of this movie feel pretty familiar. I think it would feel like this really high-stress thing where everyone feels like they have to make the most of this one night, and maybe along the way forget about the more important deeper connections that can also [happen].

Callum Turner: The night’s kind of like New Year’s Eve, Halloween, Valentine’s Day, 4th of July, wrapped into one. 

MB: Chaos.

CT: It’s chaos. 

MB: And it’s that thing where, I feel like every New Year’s, I want to do something really nice, or Halloween, I’m like, I’m going to wear this, I’m going to do this costume, and I’m going to make it really fun. That happens in like early September, and then by the time it’s October 28th, I’m like, “Oh, shit. I have to find something in my drawer.” I would never be able to plan out my One Night Only well and then inevitably be disappointed. 

The movie sets up the disappointment, but it also sets up this anticipation and the buildup, and desperation that would come with a premise like this. One of the back and forths that I love between your characters is debating whether the buildup or the after is the best part of sex. Who are you with in that argument? 

CT: I think they’ve both got points. 

MB: I think they both have a solid case [laughs]. There are 365 days of the year, we’d be absolutely fine. Humans would be fine.

CT: As celibate?

MB: [laughs] I’m just saying the build up and the after both are great [but] I don’t believe in this mandate. I don’t think it should happen. Nobody accuse me of that, please. I would move to another country! 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Refinery29 (@refinery29)

There are two different instances where Allie is being sung to on a date. In one, she is charmed by it. And in the other, she gets the ick. Do you think there’s ever an okay time to be sung to on a date?

MB: I think there’s always an okay time to be sung to. I think it’s more the lyrics of that particular song. 

CT: The first song you’re singing with him, too, right? 

MB: Yeah. He sings first and it’s lovely, and she sings along. One of my favorite lines in this whole movie is, “It’s not a duet.” It’s one of my favorite moments.

So, you’re all for being serenaded? 

MB: Yeah, it’s just that then if you turn the lyrics to something that I won’t say, that’s the end of that. 

CT: Now I have the lyrics in my head. 

MB: He has this thing where if you say a song, he has to start singing it. See, he’s sweating. 

CT: That one I’m not going to do. 

MB: We have to get a new song in his head. Um, Stand By Me! [laughs]

CT: I’m not going to do it. 

In the movie, it’s said that you don’t know somebody unless you know their pizza and their coffee orders. So, what are your pizza and coffee orders? 

CT: [Monica’s is] Cortado, oat milk. Margarita pizza, but if she’s feeling a little crazy, then she’ll throw everything on there. 

MB: Callum’s is a cappuccino, margarita pizza. 

CT: Oh, we know! 

MB: We said it like we’re really sad [but] we just locked in [laughs].

If you haven’t been keeping up on rom-coms, romance is back in a big way on TV and on film. Why do you think it left for a while and why do you think it’s back?

MB: I definitely think right now people need that catharsis. It’s kind of a wild time and even just like people trying to date in a big city, I think this movie feels cathartic for at least like friends of mine because I think they can see themselves in Allie and see that experience, like see those moments in dating where suddenly, “Oh, this turned. I got to get out of here.” Um and I think it’s just so fun to watch because of that. 

CT: And people love love. People love love! And watching people fall in love. And that’s what they get to do in this film.

One Night Only is in theaters now.

title: The Spider-Man: Brand New Day Kiss Everyone’s Talking About Is A Lesson In Consent
text:
The Spider-Man: Brand New Day Kiss Everyone’s Talking About Is A Lesson In Consent

Spoilers ahead. There’s a moment in Spider-Man: Brand New Day where Peter Parker (Tom Holland) finally gets MJ (Zendaya) back… or so he thinks. After saving her from Jean Grey’s (Sadie Sink) clutches, MJ appears to remember who he is, and the pair share a loving kiss. Soon, it’s revealed that Jean is in MJ’s mind, and Peter’s ex still has no memory of him.

When Peter is eventually reunited with the real MJ, he apologizes and admits to kissing her while she wasn’t present. Although MJ has no memory of this, fans have latched onto how Peter’s apology is a good depiction of consent. For a superhero movie to break down stereotypes of toxic masculinity and show a character like Peter Parker embracing emotions and genuinely being a good guy, it’s somewhat refreshing.

Angelique Wan, co-founder and CEO of Consent Labs, tells Refinery29 the reason it’s resonated with so many people is that it feels familiar to many people. “The scene reflects the reality that harm is not always obvious or intentional, and that conversations about consent are rarely black and white. People don’t always have all the information they need to make fully informed choices,” she says.

Peter and MJ aren’t presented as ‘heroes’ or ‘villains’ in this kiss situation, because it’s a grey area. “These nuanced, everyday scenarios make the scene so relatable and open the door to meaningful conversations about consent. It’s also worth noting that the film doesn’t extend the same nuance to Jean Grey, who acted with full knowledge of the situation,” Wan adds.

On Threads, people have praised Spider-Man: Brand New Day for including the scene where Peter apologized to MJ. At no point does he dismiss or minimize her experience, and instead, he takes responsibility. “[This] reinforces that consent is ongoing and dynamic. Just because Peter and MJ were previously in a relationship doesn’t mean consent can be assumed,” Wan explains. “The wider storyline also highlights that consent depends on informed choice, reminding us that deception or withholding important information can undermine someone’s ability to give affirmative consent.”

The expert tells R29 that stories like this on the big screen (especially ones as popular as this) can demonstrate what accountability looks like in practice. Peter’s acknowledgment that his actions could have hurt someone else, regardless of intention, sends an important message about owning your mistakes. “By centring the experiences of those affected by our actions, we can take accountability and practice relational skills that cultivate healthier relationships,” she says. “It also encourages people to speak up when something doesn’t feel right and to think about how their own actions can affect others.”

While Spider-Man is fiction, the real-world lessons it teaches young people are very real. Whether it’s about consent, respect, or healthy communication, it helps start a conversation and makes the tough conversations less awkward.

title: Copenhagen’s Wacky Shoe Trend Is All About The Big Toe
text:
Copenhagen’s Wacky Shoe Trend Is All About The Big Toe

Copenhagen Fashion Week has unofficially commenced the Fashion Month season with Spring/Summer 2027 collections and lots of striking street style. From elevated chain headwear and cargo Bermuda shorts to layered, undone hairstyles, there are tons of style ideas to take from the showgoers.

But the one viral style currently on everyone’s lips (likely on wide-eyed, jaw-dropped faces) is the new Havaianas kitten heel flip-flops, notably with big-toe caps. After being teased on the Brazilian brand’s socials, the statement sandals debuted on the Studio Constance runway on August 4. But because every brand makes heeled flip flops now, it seems that Havaianas really wanted to stand out from the rest, hence the not-so-typical concealed big toe design.

The wacky shoe of the moment is constantly evolving, from Maison Margiela’s split-toe Tabi flat revival to Tory Burch’s metal-pierced mules to Vibram’s FiveFinger utilitarian shoes. And somehow, someway, Copenhagen’s fashion It-girls are already wearing styles similar to the viral Havaianas. (Plus, just before writing this, I spotted toe-covered flip flops on the NYC subway.)

The Copenhagen street style outfits have predominantly consisted of trendy toe-ring sandals, unique peep-toe heels, and woven-fabric flats that each give peeks of summer pedicures. So maybe the solution to transitional-weather dressing — whether it’s from the summer into the fall or the winter into the spring — is not a standard flip flop or boot, but rather keeping a toe or two covered.

And wouldn’t you know it… even before Collina Strada’s Copenhagen debut on August 6, which had models strutting in cut-out toe socks in place of shoes, many runway attendees have already been pairing similar socks with their thong sandals or Havaianas flip flops. So, if the toe-cap styles are too avant-garde for you, consider DIYing socks into a faux leg-warmer look for the changing weather.  

Since the Havaianas heels aren’t available to purchase yet, shop alternatives for big-toe covered shoes, from funky cut-out heels and toe-ring sandals to strappy mules in the meantime.

title: Laser Hair Removal Changed My Confidence, But Finding The Right Place Took Years.
text:
Laser Hair Removal Changed My Confidence, But Finding The Right Place Took Years.

After being burned during a laser hair removal appointment years ago, I thought I’d never go back. Not only did the experience leave me physically scarred, but it also made me question whether laser clinics truly understood how to safely treat melanated skin. So, for years my relationship with laser hair removal was inconsistent at best — until I recently went to Milan Laser and finally experienced what laser hair removal should actually feel like. 

Why I Did It 

For years, I thought ingrown hairs were just something I had to deal with. Shaving constantly irritated my skin, waxing was painful, and no matter what I tried, I kept dealing with bumps and hyperpigmentation. By 2015, laser hair removal started feeling less like a luxury and more like a necessity. 

At the time, everyone was talking about the benefits of laser hair removal. Smoother skin, less irritation, and freedom from razor bumps. I was tired of feeling uncomfortable in my own skin, so I finally decided to try it. 

What Scared Me 

My first laser experience almost scared me away from the treatment completely. 

During an underarm session years ago, a technician accidentally burned part of my tattoo because she never asked if I had one or covered it before starting. I still have the scar today. After that, I became extremely hesitant about laser hair removal, especially because I wasn’t sure if many places truly understood how to safely treat melanated skin. 

Even though I saw some results over the years, the hair always seemed to grow back eventually. So, for nearly a decade, my relationship with laser hair removal became very on-and-off. I never found a place that made me feel fully comfortable or confident. 

The Laser Type 

Everything shifted when I went to Milan Laser Hair Removal. The moment my Black technician walked into the room, I instantly felt more at ease. I literally told her, “You don’t know how happy I am to see you,” and she smiled and said, “I’m happy to see you too.” 

It may sound small, but as a Black woman, there’s comfort in knowing someone understands your skin and your concerns. Before we even started, she asked detailed questions about my skin history, past laser experiences, and sensitivities. Nothing felt rushed. 

What also made me feel safer was learning that Milan’s technicians are licensed medical professionals and that they use the Candela GentleMax Pro laser, which is designed to safely treat a variety of skin tones, including melanated skin. 

What It Felt Like 

If you’ve never had laser hair removal before, the sensation feels like quick snaps against your skin with bursts of heat. It’s not exactly painless, but it’s far more tolerable than waxing in my opinion. 

What made the experience better at Milan was how thorough and attentive the technician was throughout the appointment. She constantly checked in to make sure I was comfortable and carefully treated every section instead of rushing through the process. The level of care honestly changed my perspective on laser hair removal. 

The Aftermath 

The results have been some of the best I’ve ever experienced. I’ve now gone back a few times, and the difference has honestly shocked me. My hair growth has slowed down significantly, my skin feels smoother, and I’m seeing far fewer ingrown hairs and dark marks. I haven’t had a session in over two months and barely see any regrowth. 

What I’d Tell A Friend 

I’d tell any friend considering laser hair removal to really do their research and find a place that understands melanated skin. That matters more than people realize. 

I’d also tell them not to settle for a rushed experience just because laser has become more common. You should feel comfortable asking questions, discussing concerns, and making sure the provider is educated on your skin specifically. And honestly? Seeing representation in these spaces matters too. 

The Cost 

One thing I appreciated about Milan Laser is their unlimited treatment model. Instead of paying for individual sessions over and over again, you pay once and can continue treatments as needed. Depending on the areas you treat, the price can range anywhere from $3,000-7,000.  

Considering how inconsistent my past experiences were, I think the investment is worth it. They also have more than 400 locations across 38 states, which makes it easy to continue treatments while traveling. 

The Verdict 

For years, laser hair removal felt intimidating to me because of my past experiences and concerns about whether providers truly understood Black skin. But this experience completely changed my perspective. The confidence boost goes beyond just being hair-free. It’s the relief of not constantly worrying about ingrown hairs, irritation, or hyperpigmentation. It’s feeling comfortable in sleeveless tops again. It’s not having to think about shaving before every trip or event. For the first time in a long time, laser hair removal finally feels worth it. 

Worth it. If you’ve ever dealt with ingrown hair, hyperpigmentation, or constantly having to think about shaving before every trip, event, or beach day, you get it. For me, laser hair was about feeling comfortable in my skin. The results have been some of the best I’ve seen in years, with significantly less hair growth, fewer ingrown hairs, and smoother skin overall. Add in the fact that I can continue treatments without worrying about paying for individual sessions, and it’s easily the best laser experience I’ve had to date. 

Skip it if you’re looking for instant gratification. Laser hair removal is a process, not a quick fix. You’ll need multiple sessions, and the results happen over time. But if you’re tired of dealing with razor bumps, ingrown hairs, and dark marks, and you’re willing to stick with it, it’s one of the best beauty investments I’ve made for myself. 

Sandy Pierre is the Branded Execution Manager at Refinery29 Unbothered and a contributing writer covering travel, lifestyle, and culture. When she’s not working on brand partnerships, she’s probably planning her next trip or curating a dinner for creatives in New York.

title: Everyone’s Obsessed With Tretinoin — But I Don’t Have A Prescription
text:
Everyone’s Obsessed With Tretinoin — But I Don’t Have A Prescription

With 38.1K posts waxing lyrical about the topical skincare medication on TikTok, there’s simply no escaping it: Tretinoin is a skincare sensation. And with each scroll, we bet you’re asking yourself, Should I get in on the hype? 

You can’t just go out and buy tretinoin; you need a prescription from a dermatologist. That said, if you’ve recently come across tretinoin online, you can infer that it’s more widely prescribed today than ever before. “I’ve been prescribing it for 15 years,” says NYC-based dermatologist Michelle Henry, MD, “but there’s been a constant uptick in interest as people have become more educated about it.”

Similar to a skincare medication like Accutane or spironolactone, tretinoin requires a doctor to write you a pharmacy prescription and teach you how to use it safely and accurately. But unlike Accutane or spironolactone (a diuretic used to treat chronic hormonal acne), tretinoin is not an acne-specific medication. It treats acne in some people, but also helps minimize the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, uneven skin tone, and reduces hyperpigmentation by blocking tyrosinase (an enzyme that helps create skin pigment) — benefits that make it transformative for a wider range of people than just those with acute acne concerns.

However, tretinoin’s rise in popularity has divided opinion among skincare experts. “I don’t think tretinoin should have gone viral on TikTok,” says Alicia Lartey, a London-based esthetician. In fact, she feels it is “irresponsible of influencers” in particular (the majority of whom she says have no background in skincare) to promote it. Why? Well, not many people are educating about the downsides, like the fact that this stuff is really strong and, of course, not accessible for everyone.

So here’s the real lowdown on prescription tretinoin — and the best alternative over-the-counter option if you want to avoid a copay.

What is tretinoin?

Tretinoin is topical retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative that increases skin cell turnover. It’s the most potent topical retinoid (more on that below). It helps to shed dead skin cells and encourage the regrowth of newer, younger skin cells. In that process, it can do a number of things. “Tretinoin helps treat acne, signs of aging, skin texture, and pigmentation,” explains Lartey. It also stimulates collagen synthesis. Consultant dermatologist Dr. Adil Sheraz adds that tretinoin can improve skin elasticity (making it smoother and more plump) and help to achieve an even skin tone.

What’s the difference between tretinoin, retinol, and retinal?

To understand exactly how tretinoin works, it pays to know about the pyramid in which it sits. Dr. Sheraz explains that tretinoin comes from the retinoid family, which includes a number of different forms, all widely available in topical skincare products. In order of potency, it goes: retinoic acid (tretinoin), retinal, retinol, then retinyl palmitate.

Prescription tretinoin sits at the top of the pyramid. “It’s the most potent form of a topical retinoid,” explains Dr. Sheraz. Compared to retinal and retinol, tretinoin is stronger and more active right away, so it works faster. There are several different Rx brands of tretinoin that dermatologists prescribe; Altreno and Retin-A are two of the most popular, but it’s also common to receive the generic version.

Below tretinoin, there’s retinaldehyde, also known as retinal. This ingredient has become increasingly popular over the years and, unlike tretinoin, it’s available over the counter. For example, Peach & Lily, Youth To The People, and Naturium all offer over-the-counter versions of retinal. Without subjecting you to a science lesson, Dr. Sheraz explains that retinal is “converted” in your skin cells so that it becomes active and is able to perform its job. This means that “[retinal] is weaker than tretinoin but stronger than retinol,” explains Dr. Sheraz. Retinal is Lartey’s preferred over-the-counter retinoid. “It also has an antibacterial property,” she says, “which is great for those managing acne.”

Underneath retinal, you’ll find retinol. “This requires multiple conversions in the skin [for it to work] and is significantly weaker than tretinoin,” says Dr. Sheraz. That’s not necessarily a bad thing. “As it’s less potent, it’s less of an irritant, and it can be bought over the counter.”

At the bottom of the retinoid pyramid, you’ll find retinyl palmitate. This is the weakest form of retinoid and often the cheapest as well. Like retinal and retinol, retinyl palmitate is present in OTC skincare, and while it’s less potent and effective, some people prefer it. “Some people get better results using a less effective form because it doesn’t irritate their skin as much, so they’re more likely to use it more often,” cosmetic chemist Randy Schueller of The Beauty Brains told R29.

Put simply, tretinoin is the most powerful of the four, though it’s available at different concentrations, some much stronger than others. “Tretinoin is available in various strengths, both as creams and gels,” explains Dr. Sheraz.

Who is tretinoin good for?

In her NYC practice, Dr. Henry prescribes tretinoin daily to a “wide range” of people. Some people use prescription tretinoin to treat adult-onset acne. “I have some patients who are oily, some who are acne prone,” explains Dr. Henry, “but some [tretinoin patients] don’t have acne at all. I have sensitive-skin patients who still want to derive those benefits who come to me for counsel on how to choose the right tretinoin formulation.”

For people who are using tretinoin for the treatment of fine lines and wrinkles, Dr. Henry says that their skin-care routine may be very simple. “If someone’s coming in for treatment of fine lines and wrinkles, they may just be on tretinoin and moisturizer and sunscreen, and that’s it,” Dr. Henry explains, adding that it’s really a case-by-case conversation. “Some patients on tretinoin are looking for a more sophisticated regimen depending on their skin concerns.”

Where can you get tretinoin?

Don’t buy tretinoin online. You need to see a dermatologist or healthcare provider for a tretinoin prescription. “It’s a prescription because of the strength and the need for someone with more expertise to guide you in using it,” explains Dr. Henry. If you have access to a dermatologist, they will likely be able to prescribe you tretinoin if you’re a good candidate.

In Dr. Henry’s New York practice, she prescribes some form of tretinoin every day. The main reason someone might not be a good candidate is if they can’t tolerate any form of retinol. However, today there are more low-strength tretinoin options. “There are lower concentrations, made with ingredients like ceramides [and] hyaluronic acid, that really make it more tolerable so that it’s an option for more people,” explains Dr. Henry. The lowest prescription concentration of tretinoin is 0.01%, which could be just fine for someone with sensitive skin.

Getting to a dermatologist might not be feasible (which we’ll speak to ahead). Some newer personalized online dermatologist services such as Skin Medicinals and Agency may prescribe tretinoin. However, an extensive digital consultation with a qualified dermatologist will always have to take place first. In some cases, it’s also recommended that you check in with your prescribing dermatologist regularly.

How do you use tretinoin?

This is where you have to be careful. If you see someone on TikTok apply tretinoin like they would a moisturizer, that is wrong and dangerous. According to dermatologists, you only need a pea-sized amount to cover your entire face. Dr. Henry recommends the “sandwich method” of application: “You put moisturizer on first, then your medicine [tretinoin], then more moisturizer.” Use it sparingly and only at night, avoiding sensitive areas, like around your nose, lips, and under eyes. “Start every other night, maybe twice a week, then slowly increase as you tolerate,” explains Dr. Henry.

In terms of the rest of your skin-care routine, Dr. Sheraz recommends that other “active” products be cut out for the time being. This includes any other retinol-based products and acids, as well as benzoyl peroxide.

Dr. Sheraz adds that when you are prescribed tretinoin, your dermatologist or doctor should always check that you have a good understanding of how to properly moisturize your skin. Though this may seem basic, retinoids can make skin feel dry, flaky, and uncomfortable, so getting your moisturizer right is a must. Look for gentle, hydrating, and soothing ingredients such as hyaluronic acid, glycerin, shea butter, and panthenol. Prescribers will also check that you’re using a broad-spectrum sunscreen in the daytime, as retinoids make skin extra sensitive to harmful UV rays.

What are the downsides of using tretinoin?

The biggest downside to tretinoin is, you probably guessed it, skin sensitivity and inflammation. “It can result in significant irritation, redness, peeling, and inflammation in certain individuals,” explains Dr. Sheraz. If you’ve tried OTC retinol in the past and you’re sensitive to it, you can expect to be sensitive if you switch to tretinoin, because it’s even stronger. It’s also important to note that due to its drying effect, tretinoin can occasionally cause eczema flare-ups. “This is why a substantial moisturizer should always be used alongside it,” says Dr. Sheraz. Another disclaimer: Like retinol and retinal, tretinoin can’t be used if you’re pregnant.

Another obvious downside is the cost.

How much does tretinoin cost?

Dr. Henry explains that it’s tricky to generalize cost because it’s an individual insurance equation. “The range could be between zero dollars and $200 depending on the insurance plan, pharmacy insurance copay, and the type of tretinoin,” explains Dr. Henry. Moreover, we have to note that access to a dermatologist is not always possible, which is a barrier to entry with prescriptions like tretinoin.

What are the alternatives to tretinoin?

If you’re looking for what would be the closest alternative to tretinoin that you can get without a prescription, it’s Differin Gel. “Differin is probably one of the most robust options you can find over the counter,” explains Dr. Henry. “That’s what I recommend.” Differin was FDA-approved in 2016 for over-the-counter use. It’s 0.1% adapalene — adapalene is an active form of retinoic acid — which is widely considered a “game changer” in the topical skincare space.

According to the aforementioned pyramid, over-the-counter retinal would also be a good alternative — not as strong as retinoic acid, but stronger and faster than retinol. If you’re super sensitive, Dr. Henry says you could also try an alternative to retinol like bakuchiol, or a serum or cream rich in peptides. “Peptides are similarly going to help stimulate collagen, get rid of fine lines and wrinkles, and help to improve facial scarring,” explains Dr. Henry, who also quotes their side effects as serendipitously good for your skin. Ultimately, trying tretinoin is not a decision to be taken lightly — no matter what TikTok videos might suggest. Thanks to its side effects and potency, it’s always recommended to consult a doctor first and work your way up with other, weaker formulas.
